deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a German prose page of lecture or study notes on ancient Hebrew history. It continues the 'Dritte Periode' (the monarchy, c. 1100–600 BC) begun on the previous page and covers Saul and the rise of David.

Content, in order:
(1) Saul did not want to stay dependent on Samuel. He offered sacrifices to Jehovah himself and consulted him directly. Samuel, embittered, tried to overthrow him and secretly anointed the youth David as king.
(2) David became a brave warrior in Saul's army and performed heroic deeds. Saul's son Jonathan was his friend. Saul came to fear him, although he knew nothing of the earlier anointing.
(3) David fled to Samuel, who took him in but soon died. David stayed in the wilderness, escaped Saul's pursuit and gathered a following of brave men. The feud lasted until Saul died in battle together with his sons, c. 1055 BC.
(4) Under Saul there was no court yet, but the Jews had become a warlike people. David at first had only a partial following, because Saul's son Ishbosheth (Isboseth) was still alive. Ishbosheth held out for 7 years and was then murdered by his own men.
(5) The next page continues: David becomes king of the whole nation at age 30, founds Jerusalem as the capital, and so on.

There are no derivations, formulas or computations to reconstruct. The hand and subject suggest student history notes, of the kind taken at Göttingen in Gauss's era. They are filed in a bundle labelled 'Lagrange1816'.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Historical slip by the note-taker or lecturer: biblically Ishbosheth reigned 2 years (2 Sam 2:10). It was David who reigned 7 years (and 6 months) in Hebron over Judah alone. The '7 Jahre' attached to Isboseth conflates the two.
As transcribed, 'mit seinen eigenen Söhnen' could be misread as Saul fighting against his sons. The sense must be that Saul fell together with his sons in battle against the Philistines (1 Sam 31).

As transcribed, 'nur von seinem eigenen Stamme Juda nicht anerkannt' is self-contradictory. The intended sense is that David was at first recognised only by his own tribe Judah, so the reading 'nicht' is suspect.

transcription_corrections: The page number '21' (in pencil, top right) is omitted from the transcription.
First line: the struck-through word before 'Saul' is uncertain. '[-Aber-]' is a guess and the cancelled word may be different.
'verrichtete[?] hier[?] mehrere Heldenthaten': the image supports 'verrichtete hier mehrere Heldenthaten'.
'Er war erst[?] hier[?] fürchtete ihn Saul' is garbled. The image suggests a clause along the lines of 'Er war erst ... ; nun fürchtete ihn Saul', but this needs re-reading.
'nur von seinem eigenen Stamme Juda nicht[?] anerkannt': 'nur' is a superscript insertion. Given the sense, the word read as 'nicht' is probably something else, or is not meant as a negation.
'Isboseth, erhielt[?] 7 Jahre': probably 'erhielt sich 7 Jahre' or a similar verb ('regierte'), with the subject being Isboseth.
'vorhergegangenen': the image may read 'vorhergegangenen' with an inserted letter (a small mark above the line). This does not change the meaning.
